regions.name: Alava
regions.flavor: Basque hill country above the upper Ebro, green valleys under wet ridges where no army stays long. Its elders bow to Pamplona or Oviedo as the year demands.

regions.name: Algarve
regions.flavor: The dry south coast and the plains behind it: fig orchards, lagoons and small harbours under Arab lords.

regions.name: Aragon
regions.flavor: A small county in the high valleys of the Aragon river, living from passes, flocks and Frankish charters.

regions.name: Asturias
regions.flavor: The mountain heart of the Christian kingdom, a wall of green hills and high ridges between the sea and the meseta. Kings are made and buried among these hills.

regions.name: Badajoz
regions.flavor: The rebel lordship of Ibn Marwan on the Guadiana, a new city and the river plains of the west. River boats and border tolls pay for its walls.

regions.name: Balearics
regions.flavor: The islands under Berber sea captains, harbours for corsairs and traders between two coasts. No emir has yet landed to stay.

regions.name: Barcelona
regions.flavor: The eastern march counties gathered in one house, from the mountain passes to the walled city on the sea.

regions.name: Bobastro
regions.flavor: The southern mountain country of Umar ibn Hafsun, ridge forts and hidden valleys in hills no emir's column has cleared.

regions.name: Castile
regions.flavor: The eastern march of the kingdom, a line of new castles from the mountains toward the Ebro. Hard frontier ground that breeds hard counts.

regions.name: Cordoba
regions.flavor: The emirate's shrunken core around the capital, still the greatest city of the west even with rebels on every road.

regions.name: Elvira
regions.flavor: The vega and the dry east under Arab lords, torn by feud between Arab and muwallad neighbours.

regions.name: Galicia
regions.flavor: Green river country of the far northwest, thick with monasteries and the shrine of Santiago. Its counts answer to Oviedo when it suits them.

regions.name: Leon
regions.flavor: The repeopled plains south of the mountains, running down to the Douro, whose fords and boats carry the border trade. Grain, mules and river tolls feed the young towns.

regions.name: Lisbon
regions.flavor: The Atlantic coast of the muwallad west, from the Mondego down to the harbour at the Tagus mouth. Northmen off the sea are an old story here.

regions.name: Merida
regions.flavor: The lands of the old western capital on the Guadiana, broken by the emirs and held together by Berber garrisons.

regions.name: Pallars
regions.flavor: The highest of the Catalan counties, shepherd hills and salt springs far up the Noguera valleys.

regions.name: Pamplona
regions.flavor: The Basque kingdom in its mountain basin, keeping the western pass of the Pyrenees. Kin to the Banu Qasi downriver, by marriage and by need.

regions.name: Seville
regions.flavor: The lower Guadalquivir under the Banu Hajjaj, Arab lords who rule the richest river plain in Iberia. Ships work the river up to the city bridge.

regions.name: Sobrarbe
regions.flavor: Steep hill country under the central Pyrenees, gorge villages and old abbeys. Raiders from the plain climb no further than its first ridges.

regions.name: Todmir
regions.flavor: The old pact-land of Theodemir on the Segura, gardens and dry hills feuding around the young capital.

regions.name: Toledo
regions.flavor: The old Visigoth heartland around the city on the Tagus rock, forever in revolt against Cordoba.

regions.name: Upper March
regions.flavor: The Ebro valley under the Banu Qasi, muwallad lords who deal with Cordoba as equals. The river carries their grain, their tolls and their wars.

regions.name: Urgell
regions.flavor: Mountain county around the see of Urgell, running down from Andorra's valleys to the dry Segre plain and its Muslim border forts.

regions.name: Valencia
regions.flavor: The watered gardens of the eastern shore along the Turia and the Jucar, rich, quiet and lightly held. River boats and sea traders carry its fruit to every port.

settlements.name: Alaon
settlements.note: Old abbey by the Noguera gorge, its charters older than the county.

settlements.name: Alicante
settlements.note: Laqant under its bare rock, a small harbour of the eastern shore.

settlements.name: Alpuente
settlements.note: Mountain town of al-Bunt, holding the dry hills toward the meseta.

settlements.name: Amaya
settlements.note: Rock fortress over the northern meseta, repeopled from the mountain valleys.

settlements.name: Andujar
settlements.note: River town where the east road crosses the Guadalquivir.

settlements.name: Armentia
settlements.note: See of the Alavese among their hills, a church and a ring of farms.

settlements.name: Astorga
settlements.note: Walled Roman crossroads restored a generation ago, gate of the roads west.

settlements.name: Badajoz
settlements.note: New city of Ibn Marwan on the Guadiana, walled by leave of a defeated emir.

settlements.name: Baena
settlements.note: Walled hill town above the campina, loyal while the emir's army is near.

settlements.name: Balaguer
settlements.note: Muslim border fort above the Segre plain, facing the mountain counties.

settlements.name: Balansiya
settlements.note: City among the watered gardens of the Turia, quiet since its Roman prime.

settlements.name: Barcelona
settlements.note: Old Roman walled city, seat of Count Wifred's house and the eastern march.

settlements.name: Baza
settlements.note: Old Basta under its dry sierra, market of the upland herders.

settlements.name: Beja
settlements.note: Plains town of Roman walls, its lords leaning to the rebels of the west.

settlements.name: Bobastro
settlements.note: Rock fortress of Umar ibn Hafsun, unreachable master of the southern hills.

settlements.name: Boltana
settlements.note: Castle village above the Ara, named in the emirs' campaign rolls.

settlements.name: Braga
settlements.note: Ancient church metropolis of the northwest, resettled under the counts of Portugal.

settlements.name: Braganca
settlements.note: Hill town of the cold northeastern marches, half empty between the raids.

settlements.name: Burgos
settlements.note: New fortress town on the Arlanzon, raised by Count Diego ten years past.

settlements.name: Cabra
settlements.note: Old see town under the sierra, fought over with the rebel of Bobastro.

settlements.name: Calatayud
settlements.note: Castle town of Ayyub on the Jalon road, second city of the march.

settlements.name: Cangas
settlements.note: First seat of the kings by the field of Covadonga, still holy to the dynasty.

settlements.name: Cardona
settlements.note: Salt mountain and castle above the frontier woods, guarded since Wifred's day.

settlements.name: Carmona
settlements.note: Hill town above the plain road, a fortress older than the emirs.

settlements.name: Coimbra
settlements.note: Mondego city of Mozarabs, lately passing between king and emir.

settlements.name: Cordoba
settlements.note: Seat of the emirs on the Guadalquivir, the great bridge and the mosque at its gate.

settlements.name: Coria
settlements.note: Walled town on the Alagon, a border hold passed between rebels and emirs.

settlements.name: Cuenca
settlements.note: Rock fort between two gorges, small and nearly impossible to storm.

settlements.name: Daroca
settlements.note: Walled town in the Jiloca gorge, on the road from the Ebro to Toledo.

settlements.name: Evora
settlements.note: Yabura of the wide plains, drawn into the rebel lordship of the west.

settlements.name: Gafiq
settlements.note: Castle of Gafiq on the road north, gate of the emir's city toward the marches.

settlements.name: Gerri
settlements.note: Salt springs and an old abbey by the Noguera, tolling the mountain road.

settlements.name: Girona
settlements.note: Walled city on the Frankish road, first stop south of the mountain passes.

settlements.name: Guadalajara
settlements.note: Bridge town of Wadi al-Hijara, holding the upper road of the middle march.

settlements.name: Guadix
settlements.note: Wadi Ash on the high road east, between the vega and the desert hills.

settlements.name: Huelva
settlements.note: Harbour between two river mouths, fishing and salt for the inland towns.

settlements.name: Idanha
settlements.note: Old see of Egitania, its walls and springs kept by a shrunken flock.

settlements.name: Ilbira
settlements.note: Madinat Ilbira in its vega, torn between Arab lords and muwallad neighbours.

settlements.name: Iria
settlements.note: Seat of the bishop who keeps the shrine of Santiago, a day's walk up the valley.

settlements.name: Jaca
settlements.note: Stone town of the Aragon valley, holding the southern mouth of the pass.

settlements.name: Jaen
settlements.note: Jayyan of the olive hills, tax house of the upper districts.

settlements.name: Jerez
settlements.note: Town of vineyards toward the bay, raided once by Northmen ashore.

settlements.name: Juromenha
settlements.note: River castle of Julumaniya, the old Marwanid refuge above the Guadiana.

settlements.name: La Seu
settlements.note: Cathedral town of Urgell under the high peaks, seat of counts and bishops.

settlements.name: Leire
settlements.note: Mountain abbey above the Aragon valley, burial house of the Pamplona kings.

settlements.name: Leon
settlements.note: Old legionary city on the meseta road, its walls repeopled from the mountains.

settlements.name: Lorca
settlements.note: Lurqa of the frontier gardens, holding the dry road toward the west.

settlements.name: Lugo
settlements.note: Old Roman town whose circle of walls still stands whole around the church.

settlements.name: Mago
settlements.note: Harbour of the eastern island, a haven for corsairs and traders alike.

settlements.name: Malaga
settlements.note: Sea town under the rebel hills, its harbour paying whoever holds the castles.

settlements.name: Mayrit
settlements.note: Fort of Emir Muhammad on the sierra road, outwork of Toledo against the north.

settlements.name: Medinaceli
settlements.note: Madinat Salim on the high pass, watching the road to the Duero wastes.

settlements.name: Merida
settlements.note: Old Roman capital on the Guadiana, punished and half emptied for its risings.

settlements.name: Murcia
settlements.note: Young city of the emirs on the Segura, capital of Tudmir since the old towns fell.

settlements.name: Najera
settlements.note: Red-cliff town on the Ebro road, in the shadow of the Banu Qasi.

settlements.name: Niebla
settlements.note: Walled town on the Rio Tinto, market of the western districts.

settlements.name: Orihuela
settlements.note: Uryula of Theodemir's old pact, the first seat of the land of Tudmir.

settlements.name: Ossonoba
settlements.note: Old see by the lagoons, now Shantamariyya of the Banu Harun.

settlements.name: Ourense
settlements.note: Town at the hot springs and the Minho bridge, rebuilt under the Galician counts.

settlements.name: Oviedo
settlements.note: City of churches raised by the kings, the royal seat behind the mountain wall.

settlements.name: Palma
settlements.note: Old Roman town on the great bay, its people answering to no emir yet.

settlements.name: Pamplona
settlements.note: City of the Basque kings in their mountain basin, wary of Franks and emirs alike.

settlements.name: Pechina
settlements.note: Sailor republic of Bajjana, grown rich on the sea trade to the east.

settlements.name: Priego
settlements.note: Mountain town of springs and mills, lately sworn to the rebel side.

settlements.name: Sagunto
settlements.note: Murbatar under the great Roman castle, its stones older than any emir.

settlements.name: Salamanca
settlements.note: Old city on the Tormes ford, thinly held on the edge of the empty plains.

settlements.name: Santarem
settlements.note: Shantarin on its cliff above the Tagus plain, granary of the lower river.

settlements.name: Santillana
settlements.note: Abbey of Santa Juliana among the sea meadows, gathering the relics of the coast.

settlements.name: Sevilla
settlements.note: River city of the Banu Hajjaj, masters of the lower Guadalquivir.

settlements.name: Sidonia
settlements.note: Shaduna of the southern hills, seat of an old district of the conquest.

settlements.name: Silves
settlements.note: Chief town of the western Algarve, red walls above a quiet river port.

settlements.name: Sintra
settlements.note: Castle on the wooded ridge above the western sea, cool and rich in orchards.

settlements.name: Siresa
settlements.note: Monastery of the high valley, schoolhouse of the little county.

settlements.name: Sopuerta
settlements.note: Iron valleys of the western Basques, named in the king's chronicle a lifetime ago.

settlements.name: Talavera
settlements.note: Walled town on the Tagus below Toledo, its rival in every revolt.

settlements.name: Tarazona
settlements.note: Old Roman town under the Moncayo, tied to the Banu Qasi river lands.

settlements.name: Toledo
settlements.note: Old Visigoth capital on its rock above the Tagus, proud and forever in revolt.

settlements.name: Tremp
settlements.note: Valley town of the Pallars counts, ringed by terraced hills.

settlements.name: Tudela
settlements.note: Ebro stronghold of the Banu Qasi, watching the river road to Zaragoza.

settlements.name: Tui
settlements.note: Old see at the Minho crossing, restored since the border pushed south of the river.

settlements.name: Ubeda
settlements.note: New town on the high ground over the Guadalquivir, work of the emirs.

settlements.name: Ucles
settlements.note: Castle of the Zannun lords on the meseta edge, half loyal to Toledo alone.

settlements.name: Ushbuna
settlements.note: Harbour city at the Tagus mouth, once burned by Northmen off the sea.

settlements.name: Vic
settlements.note: Plain of Ausona resettled under Count Wifred, a new cathedral among burned farms.

settlements.name: Xativa
settlements.note: Castle ridge above the southern huerta, key of the road to Tudmir.

settlements.name: Zamora
settlements.note: Fortress city above the Douro ford, rebuilt by King Alfonso against the raids.

settlements.name: Zaragoza
settlements.note: White city on the Ebro, greatest of the march towns, seldom obedient to Cordoba.
